headline: SIBANYE STILLWATER EAST MINE ON STRIKE — 750 Workers Walk Out; CEO Warns Montana PGM Operation May Close; 284,000 oz/yr Palladium Output At Risk
snippet: United Steelworkers members at Sibanye-Stillwater's Stillwater East mine and Columbus metallurgical complex in Montana walked off the job at 7 a.m. on September 3 after more than four months of contract negotiations failed. About 750 employees are affected; the East Boulder mine under a separate agreement continues operating. CEO Richard Stewart warned the company may have no option but to permanently close the Stillwater operation if the strike prevents implementation of a team-based wage incentive system. At roughly 446 palladium-platinum 2E ounces per day, Stillwater East accounts for meaningful non-Russian, non-South African PGM supply — the kind of disruption that historically moves palladium prices sharply.

headline: MAJOR DRILLING SMASHES QUARTERLY REVENUE RECORD — $277M In Q1 FY2027 (+22% YoY) As World's Largest Mining Driller Signals Junior Exploration Boom
snippet: Major Drilling Group International (TSX: MDI) reported record quarterly revenue of $277.3 million for Q1 FY2027 (ended July 31, 2026), up 18.7% from the prior quarter and 22.4% above the prior year. Net earnings reached $14.5 million ($0.18/share, up 43.6% YoY); EBITDA grew 15.9% to $37.2 million. South and Central American revenue surged 92.4% YoY to $95.8 million. As the world's largest drilling services provider, Major Drilling's throughput is a real-time indicator of exploration capital spending — record quarterly revenue signals that mining companies are committing capital at scale to put drill rigs in the ground across the globe.

headline: PALADIN HITS 4.25% U3O8 IN NEW ATLAS URANIUM DISCOVERY AT PATTERSON LAKE SOUTH — 7 Of 8 First-Pass Holes Hit High Grade 3.5km From Triple R, Saskatchewan
snippet: Paladin Energy (TSX: PDN) reported September 2 that its exploration program at Patterson Lake South has defined a new high-grade uranium discovery named Atlas: best hole PLS26-708B returned 8.0 metres at 1.75% U3O8, including 3.0 metres at 4.25% U3O8 from 190 metres depth; hole PLS26-718 returned 21.5 metres including 5.5 metres at 2.86% U3O8. Seven of eight first-pass holes intersected significant uranium mineralization. The Atlas discovery sits 3.5 kilometres south of the flagship Triple R deposit in the same basement-hosted structural corridor and remains open along strike and at depth. At current uranium spot above $89/lb and with Denison's Wheeler River Phoenix ISR in full-scale construction since July, the Athabasca Basin is the most active uranium exploration address on the planet.

headline: WALLBRIDGE FENELON DELIVERS 52 g/t AU IN PFS METALLURGICAL DRILLING — 3,144m Feeds Pre-Feasibility Study; Maiden Mineral Reserve Estimate On Track For Quebec High-Grade Gold Mine
snippet: Wallbridge Mining (TSX: WM) reported September 2 final assay results from seven drill holes totalling 3,144 metres at the Fenelon Gold Project in Quebec, including a high-grade intercept of 52.30 g/t gold. The program delivered 820 kilograms of mineralized material to Base Met's testing facility for bulk composite preparation and metallurgical variability testing; initial results expected Q4 2026. The drilling supports the ongoing Pre-feasibility Study and maiden mineral reserve estimate for Fenelon — the next formal milestone for this high-grade underground gold project in the Abitibi Greenstone Belt. Wallbridge is concurrently ramping up infill drilling to convert Inferred to Indicated resources for the PFS mine plan.

headline: PECOY COPPER THIRD KILOMETER-SCALE SOUTH BRECCIA INTERCEPT — 804m At 0.34% Cu Plus 42.3m At 1.01% Cu Near Surface As Peru Copper System Expands
snippet: Pecoy Copper Corp. (TSXV: PCU) released September 1 results from six drill holes at its Pecoy Copper-Gold-Molybdenum-Silver Project in southern Peru. Leading hole PEC26-072 added a third broad South Breccia intercept: 804 metres at 0.34% copper from 24 metres, including 485 metres at 0.40% copper and 101 metres at 0.56% copper plus 0.13 g/t gold. At the Northwest target, PEC26-067 returned 209 metres at 0.40% copper including 42.3 metres at 1.01% copper and 11.1 metres at 1.90% copper near surface. Three kilometre-scale intercepts now demonstrate consistent bulk-tonnage copper grades across the South Breccia system, while the near-surface Northwest high grade opens starter-pit optionality. Part of a planned 35,000-metre 2026 program.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD EXTENDS SPYGLASS ZONE TO 330m DEPTH — 9.40 g/t Au Over 4.60m In Ontario Grows High-Grade Footprint As $17.5M District Drill Program Accelerates
snippet: Dryden Gold Corp. reported September 1 that deeper drilling at the Gold Rock Camp in Northwestern Ontario extended the Spyglass high-grade gold zone to approximately 330 metres vertical depth, returning 9.40 g/t gold over 4.60 metres and growing the Spyglass footprint by roughly 110 by 50 metres. The Buccaneer zone is also expanding. Dryden has two rigs deployed under a fully-funded $17.5 million / 45,000-metre 2026 campaign targeting down-plunge extensions, new high-grade zone discovery along strike, and lower-grade continuity between high-grade shoots. Systematic depth extension of Spyglass is the result that de-risks any future underground mine study.

headline: SOLIS MINERALS SPINS FIRST DRILL AT CINTO — Maiden 2,500m Peru Copper Campaign Tests Incapuquio Fault Zone Flanked By Toquepala, Quellaveco, And Cerro Verde
snippet: Solis Minerals Ltd. (ASX: SLM / TSX-V: SLMN) commenced maiden diamond drilling at its 100%-owned Cinto Copper Project in southern Peru, launching an initial program of five holes for 2,500 metres targeting high-priority porphyry copper mineralisation. The program tests coincident geochemical and geophysical anomalies identified by IP surveying, in areas where prior surface sampling returned copper grades up to 8.7%. Cinto lies along the Incapuquio Fault Zone — the same regional structure hosting Toquepala, Quellaveco, Cuajone, and Cerro Verde, one of the world's premier copper belts. Maiden drill programs along established fault zones with that pedigree of adjacent production represent among the best risk-reward exploration profiles in the copper space.

headline: GOLD MINERS TRADING AT DECADE-LOW P/E MULTIPLES DESPITE RECORD CASH FLOWS — Why The Policy Ceiling Will Break And What Happens To Equities When It Does
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis argues that gold and silver mining stocks remain at their most attractive entry point relative to metals prices, following the January 2026 record and subsequent correction. The piece identifies the current 'policy ceiling' — Fed hike odds holding at 66% after Wednesday's ADP miss — as the final barrier before a structural re-rating: when rate-hike pricing collapses on weak Friday NFP data or a surprise Fed hold, record cash-flow leverage from current mine margins will translate into outsized equity re-ratings. Miners generating record cash flows but trading at decade-low earnings multiples represent an asymmetric opportunity for retail investors holding through the FOMC uncertainty window into the seasonally strong September-October period.

headline: THREE FED DISSENTERS STILL PUSHING FOR RATE HIKES — What The Hawkish Minority Means For Gold's Next 6 Weeks And Why The Asymmetric Setup Favours Buyers
snippet: Three Federal Reserve members are publicly advocating for additional rate hikes despite softening labour data, and this Advantage Gold analysis explains why the hawkish minority disproportionately influences gold's near-term ceiling. Even as ADP missed (38K vs 47K expected) and unemployment trends higher, dissenters keep September hike probability alive at 66%. The asymmetric setup: if dissenters prevail and September sees a hike, gold's downside is 3–5% toward $4,200; if labour data overwhelms them and the hike is paused, the short-covering rally in gold could be 5–10% as levered futures positions unwind ahead of the October seasonally strong window. With Friday's official NFP report the next major data point, the decision map governing the next 6 weeks resolves within 24 hours.
